commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[grafana] Reduce dashboard query fan-out and align live windows (#10397)

Fetch only the source groups needed by each dashboard view and share
their Arrow results across related panels. Accelerator queries return
scalar tiles and chart aggregates directly; device histories pack
repeated labels before transfer. Jobs, Runs, and RL avoid unrelated
source queries.

Floor both window bounds independently to 15-second boundaries when the
end is within 60 seconds of server time, so independently resolved panel
overrides share cached work. Original bounds are validated first; older
historical windows and ranges shorter than 15 seconds remain exact.
Absolute windows ending near now are also aligned. Rounding adds less
than 15 seconds of lag alongside the existing 20-second cache TTL.

Across two matched replays with cold bridge caches against the unchanged
live hub, median Home latency fell from 14.77 to 1.80 seconds and SQL
calls from 25 to 6. Median Jobs latency fell from 8.02 to 1.23 seconds
for 128 selected jobs. One isolated three-hour power request fell from
9.11 to 0.77 seconds with the same result. These are bridge
measurements; browser rendering, variable selectors, and external data
sources are excluded. A subsequent matched comparison of the already
optimized Accelerator page fell from 7.81 to 5.99 seconds by selecting
existing metric-family Parquet projections. RL phase filtering reduces
unused source rows but has no demonstrated page-level latency gain; both
pages retain substantial cold-query costs.

Add a dashboard replay benchmark that retains source SQL, Arrow inputs,
panel responses, and timing evidence, plus fixed-query support in the
Finelog benchmark. Finelog runtime and storage behavior are unchanged.
The [Accelerator/RL
follow-up](https://loom.oa.dev/s/m6hemaex/artifacts/finelog-dashboard-followup)
records the SQL candidates and remaining scan costs. The [report and
full
comparison](https://loom.oa.dev/s/m6hemaex/artifacts/finelog-query-report)
include output parity, timing ranges, freshness limits, and rollout
gates.

[tasks] Ingest native structural closure tasks (#10319)

Import Snowball tasks that complete a supplied assistant prefix to match
a reference JSON or delimited structure. Register pinned training and
development-evaluation splits through the existing curation catalog. The
converter uses curation row IDs and retains original identities in audit
metadata.

Use a generic PrefillHarness selected explicitly by
TaskRolloutSpec.harness. It continues the final assistant text once, can
advertise final tool schemas, and rejects interactive tools and parsed
reasoning or tool-call responses. Ordinary chat and tool-loop rendering
retain their existing behavior. The serving model chooses its tokenizer;
source token IDs remain provenance and rollout traces retain actual
model tokens.

Private verifier resources remain byte-identical and stay out of model
requests. A correct first closed outer region scores one even when later
output follows. Historical terminal-marker normalization stays outside
the semantic grader. The changed converter uses a fresh recipe version.

The 341 focused regression tests, mechanical lint, library type checks
and documentation-link checks pass. One case-sensitive filesystem check
was excluded on macOS. GPU inference for the revised harness has not
been validated.

The [trainer
companion](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/1032)
needs explicit PrefillHarness selection, genuine shared-library releases
and a real lock update.

Part of #10314.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[grug] Add the H100 pipeline foundation (#9279)

Add a stage-local JAXPP pipeline for the full MoE model blocks,
including latent/shared experts, SConv, attention positions and QB
routing. Standard 1F1B remains the default. The synthetic runner
supports the main recipe with FP32 parameters, BF16 compute and
compute-scaled MuonH; the historical BF16 capacity recipe remains
available.

Each routed expert parameter bank now shares one Frobenius norm across
its experts, matching the stacked EP model. `--expert-normalization
per_expert` provides an explicit comparison mode. `--qb-bias-mode
frozen` retains the current pending QB bias while expert and router
weights continue updating; adaptive QB remains the default. Numerical
CPU regressions cover stacked-versus-stage-local updates and both QB
state transitions.

The historical 48-layer, 65K synthetic diagnostic ran on 192 H100s with
BF16-stored parameters and per-expert normalization. Its PP24/EP8/CP1
layout placed two layers in each stage and kept expert traffic within
eight-GPU workers. It was chosen to establish capacity; no matched
PP8/EP32/CP4 Megatron comparison was performed. The README records the
later CP2 result and the differences in batch size and attention
helpers. Historical hardware results do not validate the new
normalization or frozen-QB option, and no SFT/RL quality comparison has
been run.

The affected safe suite passed 2,391 tests with four skips and five
expected failures. Focused CPU checks passed 86 tests with one skip;
required lint, full type checking, strict docs and source links passed.

#9662 is stacked above this foundation and adds checkpoint/data support,
the GB200 launcher, tracked runtime setup and bounded main-recipe
hardware validation. Before merge, this foundation still owns replacing
the positional result from `initialize_stage_local_pipeline_state`,
centralizing the repeated backend/rematerialization identifiers, and
separating the synthetic runner lifecycle in `pipeline_smoke.main`.
These deferred changes require compiled-startup transport and
optimizer-parking/warmup cleanup validation; #9662 then owns adapting
its added checkpoint/data lifecycle.

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
[eval] Recover brokered evaluations after inference preemption (#10169)

Use the existing inference broker for evaluations with one model-serving
instance, with streaming responses and worker readiness. Requests keep a
stable endpoint when GPU workers move. Pipeline-parallel gangs retain
direct serving.

When model or judge inference is unavailable, Marin stops the evaluator,
waits for readiness, and restarts it against the same output path. The
vendored Harbor and Evalchemy runtimes resume from their saved
checkpoints. Completed evaluation steps stay cached.

The broker can retry a request only before accepting response headers
from the worker. Later worker loss breaks the stream. Buffers are
bounded and abandoned requests are canceled. The broker's in-memory
queue is not durable across broker actor failure.

Uses the existing broker instead of the separate relay proposed in
#10033.

Fixes #10030.

commits.author: himanshk96
commits.message:
[datakit] Truncate Harrier documents at read time (#10310)

Harrier's embed step now keeps the first `HARRIER_MAX_RAW_TEXT_CHARS`
(100,000) characters of each document while it reads the normalized
parquet. Before, `load_file` turned whole row groups into Python dicts
and the cut happened in `_embed_shard`, after `window(4096)`. A window
could hold 4,096 untruncated documents, so worker memory grew with the
largest documents in a source.

The new reader takes each row group from `load_parquet_batch`, converts
it to Python dicts in slices of about 64 MiB of Arrow data, and cuts the
text before it yields a record. It returns a Zephyr `Reader`, so input
progress and `zephyr/records_in` still work. `embed/bytes_in` still
counts UTF-8 bytes of the truncated text, as before, and the other
`embed/*` counters are unchanged. A row with null text still raises
`TypeError`, now from the reader; normalize drops such rows, so
normalized input never reaches it. The step hash,
`EMBEDDING_ATTR_DATA_VERSION` and output paths do not change. The slice
sizing, `rows_per_chunk`, moves from the luxical pipeline to
`marin.processing.embeddings.read_chunks` so both pipelines import it
from the library; luxical reads with the same target as before.

TEI receives the same texts in the same order as on main, so the
embeddings do not change. The test source had 4 shards and 342
documents: lengths from 0 to 10x the cap, multi-byte and astral-plane
characters at the cut, and one 186 MB row group. It ran with and without
dedup attrs, whose `sorted_merge_join` depends on the reader's record
order, on 1 and 8 workers. With a hash-based fake TEI, the texts it
received and the written parquet files were byte-identical to main.

Memory was measured in one local process with a fake embedder. On 2.1 GB
of 2-20 MB documents (4 shards, 264 MB row groups, with dedup), median
peak RSS over 3 runs fell from 6,676 MB (runs 6,638-6,685) to 5,298 MB
(runs 4,824-5,651). The largest window, as Python object size, fell from
418-543 MB to 3.7-4.6 MB. The remaining peak is about 650 MB of imports
plus Zephyr's whole-row-group Arrow read, which costs 4-5x the row-group
size for each shard being read; main pays it too. With 2 shards of 10 MB
documents in 200 MB row groups, growing each shard from 200 MB to 1.2 GB
(one run per size) raised peak RSS on main from 2.5 GB to 4.8 GB; on
this branch it stayed between 2.5 and 3.0 GB. On 8 shards of 25,000
short documents, median wall time over 6 runs was 13.13 s on main and
13.03 s here. We have not run this on real normalized data or against a
live TEI server.

Harrier does not reuse luxical's `_load_records_bounded`. That loader
emits its own `embed/bytes_in` in raw characters next to Harrier's byte
count, maps null text to an empty string, and returns a plain generator,
which Zephyr does not count in `zephyr/records_in`.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[loom] Add a pm agent that maintains the goals doc and board (#10321)

Doc:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1SyDW4MF7Te3XMOfL_eT-WxX_pueEQcaLbk7eWVmteGc
Board: https://github.com/orgs/marin-community/projects/5/views/1

Add a `pm` Loom profile and a `goals` watch that runs every three hours,
around the clock, every day. Each run reads the current goals from the
goals document's Goals section, keeps the Marin high-level board's Goal
options in line with them, adds `marin` and `MarinSkyRL` issues that
belong to a goal, and moves board items to match issue and pull-request
state. It then rewrites the document below its `Status` heading; people
own the text above it. `watch_state` records what the agent wrote and
changed, so it does not undo later human edits.

Renaming a goal keeps its Goal option ID, so its items keep the goal,
and `board-goals` refuses to remove an option that items still have.
Loom's session GitHub tokens cannot write organization projects, so the
profile reads a fine-grained token from the `LOOM_PM_BOARD_TOKEN`
secret. With that token, `board-set` moved #10043 to Done and
`board-goals` rewrote the current options without changing any item's
goal. Adding a new issue and renaming an option have not run against
GitHub yet.

The Docs API rejects the VM's cloud-platform metadata token, so
`loom-vm` gets token-creator on itself and the session impersonates it
for a documents-scoped token. Apply the `marin` IAM stack before rolling
out Loom.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[marina] Reduce shared Postgres load and query latency (#10383)

Keep Echo chunk IDs stable across MarinMirror corpus rebuilds and skip
writes when mirrored content is unchanged. The importer previously used
build-local SQLite row numbers, causing hourly runs to upsert 80–92k of
103k chunks. The content digest includes metadata and vectors, so later
changes to either still trigger writes. The migration preserves IDs of
retained chunks, removes duplicate copies, and sets a 5% autovacuum
scale factor on `chunks` and `repository_file_chunks`.

Replace Evaldash's `FOR SHARE` reader lock with a read-only
repeatable-read transaction, keeping catalog generations and records
consistent while ingestion commits. Batch source verification updates,
filter the requested cohort before hashing model configurations, and
precompute model and filter metadata with each catalog snapshot.
Metadata requests reuse those lists and read current archive flags;
synchronous metadata work runs in a worker thread
([incident](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/804)). Reuse bounded
role-isolated Marina query pools with session cleanup and cap Grafana's
metadata pool at 10 open and 2 idle connections.

On local PostgreSQL 16, reordering 1,000 unchanged activity chunks fell
from 1,000 upserts plus 1,000 deletes to zero writes (0.859s to 0.023s).
Batching 1,024 Evaldash verification updates reduced statements from
1,024 to 8 and median time from 0.505s to 0.386s. With 14,710 production
catalog records loaded in memory, the September 24 panel computation
fell from 617ms to about 64ms with identical output. These local
measurements do not establish production latency gains.

Evaldash revision 5 carries the Evaldash changes. Echo still requires an
explicit package release: pause its hourly trigger and drain existing
executions before the identity migration; older sync writers cannot
overlap it. The first new sync fills the content digests once. Runtime
and Grafana changes use their separate deployment workflows. See the
[Echo release
procedure](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/822d17c052/infra/marina/apps/echo/README.md#sync-job),
[Evaldash release
procedure](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/822d17c052/infra/marina/apps/evaldash/README.md#release),
and [Marina runtime
deployment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/822d17c052/infra/marina/README.md#base-runtime-deployment-and-first-cutover).

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[grug] Add an AMD Grug attention layer benchmark for one or more GPUs (#9883)

Add `lib/levanter/scripts/bench/bench_grug_attention_amd.py`, which
times one Grug attention layer on one or more AMD GPUs. It exits unless
the backend is ROCm: it targets the AMD Pallas-Triton kernel, and the
NVIDIA FA4/CuTe kernels need packed segment IDs that its inputs do not
have.

For each mask (2048-token sliding window, global causal) and each
implementation passed to `--impl`, it reports forward and
forward-plus-backward time and the max absolute output difference
against the first implementation.

With `--sweep --sweep-part fwd|dq|dkv` it times a grid of tile sizes,
warps and stages for one of the three Pallas-Triton flash kernels
(forward, dQ, dK/dV) and keeps the defaults for the other two.
`--block-q`, `--block-k`, `--num-warps` and `--num-stages` replace that
kernel's default values for one axis of the grid.

TFLOP/s counts only the FLOPs the mask needs over the allowed (query,
key) pairs. Each time is the median of ten 0.2 s windows after a 1 s
warmup. Results are printed as `RESULT {json}` lines.

`--num-devices N` runs on the first N GPUs with the batch sharded over
an explicit `data` mesh axis, as in Grug training. `--batch` is per GPU,
so the global batch is N times it; TFLOP/s are reported in total and per
device.

Defaults are the June per-GPU shape at global batch 64 on 8 GPUs: 8 x
4096 tokens, 20 query heads, 5 KV heads, head_dim 128, bf16.

```bash
python lib/levanter/scripts/bench/bench_grug_attention_amd.py --impl reference xla_flash gpu_pallas_triton_flash
python lib/levanter/scripts/bench/bench_grug_attention_amd.py --sweep --sweep-part dkv --block-q 64 128 --num-stages 1
python lib/levanter/scripts/bench/bench_grug_attention_amd.py --num-devices 8
```

Forward plus backward time on one MI350X with jax 0.11.1 and the ROCm
10.1 plugin (job 460980):

| Mask | reference | xla_flash | gpu_pallas_triton_flash |
|---|---|---|---|
| window 2048 | 18.84 ms (96 TF/s) | 22.66 ms (80 TF/s) | 6.74 ms (268
TF/s) |
| causal | 20.89 ms (115 TF/s) | 22.89 ms (105 TF/s) | 10.02 ms (240
TF/s) |

In the same job, the dK/dV sweep with the window mask ran all 36
configs. The default tile, 128 queries x 64 keys with 4 warps and 1
stage, was the fastest at 6.80 ms.

On one Vultr MI355X node with jax 0.11.0 in the TheRock 7.14 container
(job 11645), 8 GPUs at global batch 64 run within 1% of one GPU at batch
8, so per-device throughput holds under batch sharding. Forward plus
backward, TF/s per GPU:

| Mask | GPUs | reference | xla_flash | gpu_pallas_triton_flash |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| window 2048 | 1 | 15.60 ms (116 TF/s) | 21.47 ms (84 TF/s) | 5.87 ms
(307 TF/s) |
| window 2048 | 8 | 15.78 ms (114 TF/s) | 21.77 ms (83 TF/s) | 5.91 ms
(305 TF/s) |
| causal | 1 | 15.08 ms (160 TF/s) | 21.57 ms (112 TF/s) | 9.19 ms (262
TF/s) |
| causal | 8 | 15.24 ms (158 TF/s) | 21.81 ms (110 TF/s) | 9.23 ms (261
TF/s) |

On 8 GPUs, the default dK/dV tile was again the fastest of the six block
sizes swept (block_q 64 or 128, block_k 32, 64 or 128, 4 warps, 1
stage), at 5.91 ms.

The script imports `TritonFlashBlockSizes` and
`pallas_triton_flash_attention` from
`levanter.grug.attention._amd_pallas_triton_flash`, which #10014 added.

Part of #9812

[levanter] Charge datastore reads only after budget approval (#10340)

A rejected cross-region budget charge marked the datastore as charged,
so a later read-only open in the same process could skip the guard. Mark
the path only after the size lookup and transfer charge succeed. Recheck
under the lock so concurrent opens still charge once.

then retries after increasing the limit and confirms exactly one charge.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
Vendor SkyRL behind an isolated executable Move the supported SkyRL runtime into `vendor/skyrl` and route Marin RL artifacts through its isolated `marinskyrl` executable. Source changes can land with Marin while SkyRL's Torch/CUDA dependencies retain their own resolution and lock. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Marin["Marin environment · root uv.lock"] Experiment["RL experiment / artifact graph"] --> Adapter["marin.rl.skyrl"] end subgraph SkyRL["vendor/skyrl · independent uv.lock"] Code["cloud/ · marinskyrl/
skyrl-train/ · skyrl-gym/
templates · upstream provenance"] --> CLI["marinskyrl executable · CPU environment"] end Adapter -->|"launch YAML / child process"| CLI CLI -->|"verified source + assets + lock"| GPU["Iris GPU task
editable SkyRL + frozen Megatron/vLLM profile"] GPU --> Output["Distributed checkpoints / HF policy export"] Output --> Eval["Marin evaluation artifact"] ``` Marin clears its Python environment selection at the subprocess boundary; the launcher reuses its own CPU environment. GPU workers install the bundled source and frozen profile without cloning the fork. Ray ports use Iris allocations or task-local kernel selection on Kubernetes, so concurrent jobs can share a host. The runtime identity hashes the current source, assets, and lock, so ordinary vendor edits work without migration restaging. Workers verify each bundled file against that identity. SkyRL may depend on Marin inside its nested environment; Marin accesses SkyRL only through the executable. Remove the obsolete `config/external/MarinSkyRL` pin and updater entry. Retain Megatron/vLLM, OPD, Grug, task execution, generation, and checkpoint export. Drop `skyrl-tx`, the unused replay buffer, unsupported launcher registrations, and files outside the declared entrypoint/import/asset closure. A captured local patch preserves math grading and nested runtime bundling. Use compensated reward aggregation to reduce sensitivity to asynchronous evaluation completion order. Preserve the upstream license and an independent-lock CI lane that audits the built wheel against the current checkout. The migration script can refresh the vendored tree as the fork advances. It captures upstream and active work, replays all local vendor changes with a three-way merge, and rebuilds the stacked PR report. A preview leaves the checkout unchanged; apply rejects intervening edits. Conflicts can be resolved in the candidate and saved as a normalized patch for the next refresh. ```mermaid flowchart TB Fork["Fork main + all open PRs
recently active open issues"] --> Snapshot["Snapshot
source, patches, discussions"] Snapshot --> Baseline["Prune + replay local vendor changes"] Local["Current vendor/skyrl edits"] --> Baseline Baseline --> Decision["Inspect candidate / resolve conflicts"] Decision --> Vendor["Apply vendor/skyrl baseline
save patch for next refresh"] Snapshot --> Transplants["Separate PR branches
preserve stack parents"] Transplants --> Publish["Publication after merged cutover
and unchanged source identities"] ``` Open PR changes remain separate from the baseline. Publication previews issue transfers and draft PR creation; execution requires this cutover PR to be merged with the candidate's fork revision and patch hashes, plus unchanged fork main and PR heads/bases. Incomplete transplants require an explicit disposition. Reviewed adaptations can restore needed tests and docs or relocate changes into Marin; the tool captures their patch hashes and replays all selected stacks before pushing draft PRs. Retries reject changed source identities, patch bytes, destination heads, or published text. Include the GPU-qualified Snowball layout from [#10163](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10163): separate reference nodes, recomputation, optimizer offload, and per-role geometry validation. Remove the obsolete FSDP profile. The nested runtime uses published Marin packages and the current harness API. A dedicated updater advances those libraries within the nested version constraints, checks imports and constructor keywords in the isolated environment, and restores the lock on failure. The [migration guide](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/forks-merge-marinskyrl/docs/dev-guide/skyrl-migration.md) covers refreshes, dependency updates, train/export/resume/evaluate acceptance, and rebasing PRs that edit the deleted fork pin. Move the CPU CatCount, OPD, Grug/Megatron, and asynchronous GPU CatCount schedules into Marin, preserving their metric gates, weekly/manual cases, failure artifacts, and cleanup. Run GPU CatCount from the checked-out Marin revision instead of cloning Marin and rewriting a fork pin. Point new dashboard results at Marin while preserving fork history. The nested executable boundary follows [Harbor #10287](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10287) and [Evalchemy #10288](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10288).

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
Vendor Evalchemy with an isolated evaluation runtime

Vendor Evalchemy under `vendor/evalchemy` with all 42 benchmark dataset
generators, active graders and resume support. Remove benchmark pages,
database tracking, reporting, original model providers, standalone rollout
drivers and unused evaluator configurations. Keep the prompt processing and
scoring code used by Marin.

Evalchemy has its own `uv.lock` and environment outside the root workspace's
dependency resolution. Marin invokes its CLI in a child process. FineStore and
Rigging resolve from checkout-local sources so changes can land atomically.
Replace the active fork pin and refresh machinery, and retire the fork's
nightly dashboard lane while preserving its history.

Fetch larger canonical benchmark datasets from full Hugging Face commit SHAs.
Stage shared copies under repository/revision/file keys using the configured
scratch storage, with leases and completion markers. Standalone runs can use
the native HF cache without origin probes or an explicit local/object-store
destination. Direct HTTP files use the same staging mechanism with an explicit
publisher version; downloads stream without additional content hashing. The
NUPA-Loose and NUPA5K-Loose benchmarks also read from the shared cache. Preserve
dataset ordering, prompts, benchmark test cases and sample identities; keep tiny
datasets and custom snapshots bundled. The default Iris bundle is 14.4 MiB,
within the deployed 25 MiB limit.

Immutable evaluation caches track evaluator inputs, portable configuration
and the dependency lock. Evaluation records retain broader adapter and
local-library provenance. Dated `eval-policy-*` configurations that select
external Evalchemy commits fail before writing configs or starting jobs.
Historical policies and grader replay scripts require the corresponding
pre-vendoring Marin checkout.

Remove benchmark generators and their development tooling, inputs,
locks, and tests, along with the website, results viewer, benchmark
publishing, hosted result sharing, and unused registry snapshot.
Prebuilt datasets remain available through Hugging Face, the Harbor
registry, and local task trees.

All Harbor launches execute the checked-out source. Historical cohort
metadata continues to validate saved records. Evaluation provenance
records a combined source digest for Harbor, its Marin driver, and local
Rigging and FineStore dependencies alongside the Harbor lock digest. CI
checks the independent lock for freshness.

Preserve packaged runtime assets in Iris bundles and exclude vendored
unit tests by default.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[eval] Check in the September evaluation campaign (#9569)

Check in the model, evaluator, and launcher configurations for the
September 2026 evaluation campaign, together with the runtime fixes
needed for serving, retry, resume, and coverage. The launcher validates
external pins, writes immutable effective-config snapshots, and accepts
an optional submitter-controlled version label. That label does not
attest policy conformance.

Harbor results are bound to the full model and hosted judge
configurations, dataset, policy, runtime, and task limit. Resume checks
this identity before submission and reuse. A changed checkpoint under
the same served name is rejected, as are existing roots without
model-bound provenance. Recovery retries known infrastructure failures
and unscored trials while retaining scored outcomes and unknown errors.

The frozen Harbor runtime pins 94b118022fe3e677784a638daf33d57a836fa5fe
and includes the Tau3 adapter. The Evalchemy lock and generated pin
match Marin's external dependency configuration.

SWE-bench uses the native Mini-SWE adapter from merged [Harbor
#232](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/232) and
[#233](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/233). Its
32,768-token context includes the prompt and reply together. Mini-SWE
counts the rendered prompt through the serving tokenizer, including
tools and the generation prefix, and caps the reply within the remaining
budget and server window. Harbor loads Mini-SWE's base configuration
before applying overrides and selects its batch agent, which saves the
trajectory on context exhaustion without prompting. Harbor can then
verify the existing patch.

Sotopia uses the packaged agent from merged [Harbor
#231](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/231). Judge
failures become verifier infrastructure errors. The Marin agent wrappers
and their harness dependencies are removed. Sotopia's native generation
still does not enforce its declared context budget, so those results
cannot establish conformance to the 32K context policy.

Part of #9566.

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[haliax] Let ragged_dot pick a Triton kernel family explicitly (#10099)

`ragged_dot` accepts `implementation="triton_group_grid"` and
`"triton_tile_map"`, which run one Pallas-Triton kernel family whatever
the GPU. `RAGGED_DOT_IMPL` takes the same values, which is how the MoE
layers select it. `"triton"` and `"auto"` keep the per-GPU default:
tile-map on AMD Instinct, Hopper and data-center Blackwell, and
group-grid on every other GPU, such as A100, L4, A6000 and consumer
Blackwell (sm_120). Neither family has been measured on those GPUs, so
their default does not change.

Tile-map on those GPUs, which this opt-in now allows, used the
group-grid blocks (128x128x32, 4 warps, 4 stages). On H100 those blocks
made tile-map 0.78-0.89x of group-grid at the Mixtral-like shape (G=8,
4096x14336) at M=16384. A sweep of 96 configs on H100 picked one config
per layout among configs whose operand stages fit in 99 KiB of shared
memory. 99 KiB is the per-block limit on sm_86, sm_89 and sm_120; A100
allows 163 KiB. Per call in bf16, against group-grid with its own
blocks:

| Layout | Blocks (m x n x k), warps, stages, group_m | June, G=32,
M=16k and 128k | Mixtral-like, G=8, M=16k and 64k |
|---|---|---|---|
| fwd | 128x256x32, 8, 4, 8 | 1.12-1.16x | 1.18-1.83x |
| dlhs | 128x256x32, 8, 4, 1 | 1.21-1.59x | 1.39-2.22x |
| drhs | 128x128x32, 4, 3, 8 | 1.00-1.08x | 1.03-1.18x |

The Iris jobs are `/dev/ragged-dot-group-grid-vs-tile-map` and
`/dev/ragged-dot-generic-config-sweep`, both on H100. The 1.83x and
2.22x peaks come partly from group-grid slowing down once a group's rows
exceed L2 (`/dev/ragged-dot-group-grid-l2-cliff`), which a separate PR
will address. In the same grid, the tuned H100 configs remained the
best, so this PR leaves the tuned tables unchanged.

The ragged_dot tests pass on one H100 (43 passed, 30 f32 cases skipped
for TF32; `/dev/ragged-dot-family-opt-in-tests-3`) and in the CPU
interpreter. A new GPU test checks the value and gradients of each
explicit family against XLA.

commits.author: muchanem
commits.message:
[shellbox] Run local commands below their host process's CPU priority (#10156)

Local sandbox commands now start at niceness 10 above the host process,
so
CPU-bound commands compete less with the process that drives their
machines.
With the local backend, solver and grader commands run in the
coordinator's
own pod. In a Taskforge validation run on cw-rno2a, sandbox and ShellSim
starts
in a 4-CPU coordinator grew to 5-32 s while long CPU-bound solver
commands
ran. With 16 busy-loop commands pinned to two CPUs, creating and running
a new
machine took 484 ms at p50 and 916 ms at p99 at equal priority, and 360
ms and
383 ms with this change. Sizing the coordinator's CPU request stays the
main
remedy.

The local-machine suite passes as root on cw-rno2a under the PRIVILEGED
profile (35 passed, 2 skipped after merging main), except
`test_a_python_environment_runs_its_own_interpreter_and_locked_packages`,
which also fails on main there (offline resolution with a fresh uv
cache). Part of #10119.

commits.author: muchanem
commits.message:
[shellbox] Let local machines write system directories copy-on-write (#10155)

LocalMachineFactory takes
system_directories=SystemDirectories.COPY_ON_WRITE,
which overlays /usr, /bin, /sbin, /lib*, /etc and /opt in each machine
with a
writable layer of its own. Commands see the host's files plus their
machine's
writes; the writes persist across that machine's commands, close()
discards
them, and the host never changes. The default stays READ_ONLY.

Generated Taskforge tasks that write under /opt (a seeded generator
written by
a setup command, task resources shipped there) failed on the local
backend and
passed in gVisor. With this mode they run locally.

Files the host mounts inside an overlaid directory are bound back
read-only
after the overlay, because overlayfs shows only the directory's own
filesystem; without this, a Kubernetes pod's /etc/resolv.conf and
/etc/hosts
would revert to the image's copies. The workdir may lie in an overlaid
directory, and upload and download there, like an upload to /, go
through the
sandbox as a tar stream so they see the machine's layer. These transfer
commands run in a fixed environment that MachineSpec.env does not
change, and
the downloaded stream is treated as untrusted: it must start with a
regular
file or directory, hard links must stay inside it, and devices are
refused. A
download of / from a copy-on-write machine is refused. The factory's
startup probe mounts
the overlays, so a host without overlayfs, or with a temporary directory
on
overlayfs, raises SandboxUnavailable. Writes keep file permissions, so
changing
root-owned directories needs a root host process, as on Iris under the
PRIVILEGED profile.

On cw-rno2a, the layer adds no measurable cost per command (18.1 ms with
/opt, /usr and /etc overlaid, 18.2 ms without), and two concurrent
commands of
one machine share its layer correctly.

The local-machine suite passes as root on cw-rno2a under the PRIVILEGED
profile, except
`test_a_python_environment_runs_its_own_interpreter_and_locked_packages`,
which also fails on main there (offline resolution with a fresh uv
cache). The copy-on-write tests skip on non-root hosts. After the review
fixes, the local-machine suite gave 34 passed, 2 skipped and that same
failure as root on cw-rno2a. Part of #10119.

commits.author: gonzalobenegas
commits.message:
Acquire pinned Harbor Hub releases through the curation cache (#10198)

Acquire pinned Harbor Hub releases through the existing cached
source-download stage. Preserve each task's original archive bytes,
verify its extracted contents with Harbor's native content hash, and
record the resolved task references in a release manifest.

The Hub client is bundled with the Harbor evaluation framework. This
implementation reuses Marin's pinned, isolated Harbor environment and
command builder. Acquisition itself does not run agents or graders.

Like HF acquisition, download the complete release before curation
sampling and retain native files for dataset-specific parsing.
HarborHubSource uses the existing read(StoragePath, ConversionContext)
callback, download cache, and local-input overrides. Retries reuse
completed archives. Cache identity includes the release, acquisition
code, and pinned Harbor commit. Harbor resolves release membership;
per-task content verification is independent of that resolution.
Dataset-level scoring files remain unsupported.

Seven focused cases pass locally. Pipeline tests run in ordinary CI; the
three SDK-dependent acquisition cases run manually in the pinned Harbor
environment and skip in ordinary CI. A live smoke test downloaded the
pinned Skill2Env task task_api-design-reviewer_jdkbai64, verified its
native content hash, and read the resulting archive through the existing
pipeline custom-reader interface, producing one row with the task
prompt. This validates acquisition and reading for one task;
full-release acquisition, remote-storage acquisition, runnable
conversion, and grading were not exercised by this smoke test.

Part of #9630.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[grug] Update context-sharding tests for the local token flatten (#10313)

After #10145, each device flattens its own block of rows and sequence
shard. Under context parallelism, expert-parallel group `c` now holds
sequence shard `c` of all rows. Before, it held the whole rows `c` and
`c + 2`. Three tests in `tests/test_moe_context_sharding.py` compared
against the old layout, and `unit (marin 3/3)` failed on main at
fe4c536df. The references now give each device the same tokens in the
same local order as the context mesh. The updated tests fail against the
model before #10145.

The CI test selector reads only module-level imports. These tests and
`experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/test_context_parallel.py` import the hero
model only in a subprocess script, so the CI for #10145 did not run
them. A module-level import in each file now records that dependency.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[rolloutengine] Run managed agents on chat endpoints (#10264)

Managed agents can now run on chat endpoints through one `run_task`
call. A registered harness is the agent program, the model is its
endpoint, and a task with `NoGrader` holds open-ended work. This is part
of #10165.

`ChatModel` in `rolloutengine.chat` uses `TraceMode.MESSAGES` with an
OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, such as vLLM, SGLang, or GLM. Prompt
options replace its `max_tokens` and `extra_body` keys. The `model`,
`messages`, `stream`, and `n` fields are reserved, including within
`extra_body`. A response without `usage` fails one model attempt instead
of raising a `RolloutContractError` that stops the caller. The next
request sends back only `role`, `content`, `tool_calls`, and
`reasoning_content`; a refusal goes into `ModelTurn.metadata`.

`HarnessContext` now holds `limits` so an `AgentHarness` program can
read them without a `ModelSession`. Three failure paths are corrected:
`check` rejects `output_paths` without a task machine, which previously
produced `outputs={}` without an error; an agent that ends with a
`CancelledError` before the engine stops it, for example from a
cancelled child task or a cancel of its own task, fails its attempt
instead of making `run_task` raise `CancelledError` (in #10203, a cancel
of the agent task by another task propagated); and `RolloutInterrupted`
and `GradedRolloutInterrupted` survive pickling with their rollout,
operation, and grade. `RolloutFailure.diagnostics` also retains the
error message and notes that pickle drops. Previously, Zephyr replaced
the exception with a `ZephyrWorkerError` retaining only its type and
message.

`docs/references/task-rollouts.md` now has a short “Run an agent”
section.
